findings.finding: The board raised the interim dividend 3.6% to a 'record' 2.85p and the chairman wrote 'Our very long record of dividend increases continues', which signals a 50th consecutive annual increase at the final. H1 cash was GBP70.8m on GBP36.9m of operating cash inflow, so it is affordable even with cover near 1x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raised dividends at the Oct 2024 prelims (+3.95%), the Oct 2025 prelims (-2.34%) and the Mar 2026 interims (+1.26% on this stage's window). The raise is expected and has not decided the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: AJ Bell already wrote that the net-cash balance sheet should help keep the streak alive, and the stock yields about 7% at 128p on an 8.8p+ dividend. If the market doubted the increase, the yield would be wider and the shares would be at the July low (118.6p) rather than 8% above it. The residual value is the small chance of a larger-than-token raise, set against a tail risk of a hold.
findings.independence: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/group/news/input-costs-and-tough-markets-take-toll-james-halstead (AJ Bell, 22 Jul 2026: the dividend streak dates back to 1974 and the balance sheet should help maintain it)

findings.finding: Auditor BDO asked for two more weeks to finish FY26 audit procedures, pushing the results from 1 Oct to 14 Oct. The company says it has 'not been informed of any material audit issues'. On a company that 'carries significant stock' and took extra volume, the open item is most plausibly inventory, with a small tail risk of a provision or a presentational adjustment in the audited numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior audit delay in the JHD RNS record back to 2023. The stock rose 0.95% on the day of the delay notice (28 Sep), so the market did not read it as a warning.
findings.why_not_priced: The market priced it as benign: the stock rose on the notice and has held 124-129p since. If an adjustment were expected, the shares would have fallen on 28 Sep and drifted lower into the print. The finding is the unpriced tail, which is why it is sized small with a long negative range.

findings.finding: The FY27 outlook starts from a weak base. The company's own TU says June UK sales were 'driven by purchases in advance of price increases in July', so July-September volume was pulled forward. The input-cost spike it absorbed has not clearly unwound: Brent was ~$89-93 in late August, and Kalshi weekly contracts for 9 and 16 Oct priced 63-69% odds of Brent above $99.99. Peer Forbo said raw-material, energy and transport costs 'prevented margin improvements' in H1 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: JHD's guidance is qualitative and moves come on the TUs: the July 2025 and July 2026 TUs that downgraded profit fell 5.1% and 5.2%; the July 2024 TU rose 9.0%. The Oct 2025 prelims' 'expects further progress in FY26' outlook fell 2.34%, and the profit fell anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The shares bounced from 118.6p to 139.6p in August and gave most of it back to ~128p, so there is no visible pricing of either a margin recovery or a second leg down. If the market expected a soft Q1 from the pre-buy, the shares would trade nearer the July low. The oil-to-margin link is macro-to-company transmission, which the company has confirmed for FY26 but not for FY27, so this is sized small.
